title: expand_dns_name hands g_snprintf a size one larger than its chunk, so the terminator can land one byte past
live_proof: absent at the pin, and this one is a worked example of why ancestry and added-line probes are not liveness tests. v4.6.8:epan/dissectors/packet-dns.c reads 'snprintf(np, maxname, ...)' at :1677, :1689 and :1703 -- the FIXED form -- with the allocation 'np=(char *)wmem_alloc(scope, maxname)' at :1619. The triage script reported DEFECT-LIVE because upstream renamed g_snprintf to snprintf, so none of the fix's added lines match verbatim; the pinned source refutes that. A fix-reversal. The pre-fix shape is 'g_snprintf(np, maxname + 1, ...)' at 5a560f3f6a^.
object: the printable DNS name buffer, maxname bytes in the packet scope
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial row.
shape: a size one larger than the chunk permits a one-byte write past it
allocator_layer: block_fast -- the packet scope (wmem_packet_scope()); the firing bound is wm_narrow()'s.
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. Reduced to the single byte at index maxname -- the one a size of maxname + 1 permits and a size of maxname does not. The name expansion itself is dropped.
distinguishing: the smallest crossing in the corpus: exactly one byte, and a write. If any arm were going to miss a crossing by rounding or alignment, this is the row where it would show.

spatial.oracle: fault at the labelled write probe
spatial.note: Every arm of this harness narrows a wmem allocation to its request -- ports/wireshark/wmem/src/shared/wmem-port-hooks.h:11-15, wm_narrow(), unconditional under WM_DOMAIN -- so a spatial crossing faults on all of them and this case does NOT discriminate the chunk port. Established by case 13, whose completion predictions the run refuted; these four are pre-registered with that correction already applied. PREDICTION REFUTED BY THE RUN, 2026-10-05: this arm was pre-registered with cause 5, the LOAD access fault. A bounds violation on a STORE raises cause 7, and the run read 7 at exactly the predicted write-probe pc. Corrected to 7. The two read rows (13, 14, 15) do read 5, so the pre-registration was right about the probe and wrong about load-vs-store.

native-detect.oracle: NO ASan report: the crossing stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks to poison. A silent arm needs its own positive control -- a crossing past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- before it means anything.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.

status: MEASURED 2026-10-05 under QEMU on BOTH builds (WM_CHUNKS=ON and OFF): cause 7 at the labelled WRITE probe, with the pc equal to the probe address the run resolved from the image. 12/12 arms on each build, runner exit 0, with case 11 in the same runs as the temporal regression control reading cause 24, and the suite's negative control reporting 12/12 oracles FAIL as they must. Bundles: results/20261005-qemu-spatial-5-{ON,OFF}/. A fix-reversal. Both arms read the same because wm_narrow() narrows every wmem allocation on every arm, so this harness has no malloc-granular arm and the row does not discriminate the chunk port. PoisonCap and CheriBSD are unmeasurable here; native-detect is declined, not pending -- see the corpus README. N = 1 per cell.
